newsitem.title: UK: Baltic Exchange will not propose new restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Exchange will not propose new restructuring.

text.p: The Baltic Exchange said Thursday it will not put forward new restructuring plans at its annual general meeting despite concerns expressed by major shareholders.
Baltic chief executive Jim Buckley said the board had met representatives of major shareholders on Wednesday who had approached the shipping market's management.
"There will be nothing between now and the AGM," he said when asked if the Baltic would draw up new plans as a result of the meeting.
The 26 largest shareholders met earlier this week to discuss divisions over rival proposals to pay out a special dividend on Baltic shares.
The Baltic recently dropped plans to propose a 100 pounds stg dividend at the AGM on July 16 because it decided it would not gain sufficient support.

In February it rejected a proposal by management consultants Deloitte & Touche to pay out a dividend of between 200 and 250 stg. The Baltic argued the payment would cost it all its cash savings currently bringing in investment income and drastically reduce the size of the institution.
Some Baltic insiders have speculated that the shareholders' group asked the board to implement much of the Deloitte plan.
Buckley declined to comment, but added: "All I can say is that was not what was discussed between us."
He said there was not time now to draw up new papers for the AGM, but said the meeting would give shareholders the opportunity to raise any issue.

Peter Kerr-Dineen, chairman of shipbroking firm Howe Robinson, who called the shareholders' meeting, said: "There is absolutely no comment to be made." -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
